title: Breeding Exercise 1: Inheritance
lessonSummary: Great! Your child class inherits everything from its parent.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: a child class inherits a method.
Write the class Horse with `__init__(self, name)` and `introduce(self)` (prints I am Blitz.) and the child class Racehorse(Horse) with only `pass`. Create Racehorse("Blitz") and call `introduce()`.

tasks.instruction: The class Horse is given. Write Jumper(Horse) with a **new** method `start(self)` that prints Stella leaves the starting box. (name from `self`). Create Jumper("Stella") and call `introduce()` first, then `start()`.

validation.expected:
I am Stella.
Stella leaves the starting box.

tasks.instruction: The classes Horse, Racehorse(Horse) and Jumper(Horse) are given. Create Racehorse("Blitz") and check with `isinstance` whether it belongs to Horse and whether it belongs to Jumper. Print both results on two lines.

lessonSummary: Nice! Children may do things differently from their parents.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: an overridden method.

validation.expected:

validation.expected:

Stella jumps the fence.

title: Breeding Exercise 3: super() and __init__
lessonSummary: Well done! You connect parent and child with super().

tasks.instruction: Run this example: a constructor with super().

The class Horse is given. Write Racehorse(Horse) with `__init__(self, name, speed=30)` that sets the name via `super().__init__(name)` and stores `speed`. Create Racehorse("Blitz", 45) and print exactly Blitz 45.
The class Horse is given. Write Jumper(Horse) with `__init__(self, name, height=50)` and `super()`. Create Jumper("Stella") without a second value and print exactly Stella 50.

The classes Horse and Racehorse (with an overridden `run`) are given. Write Champion(Racehorse) that overrides `run`: first `super().run()`, then a second line Blitz is a master!. Create Champion("Blitz") and call `run()`.

validation.expected:
Blitz sprints down the track.
Blitz is a master!

tasks.instruction: Run this example: the same method, three classes.

validation.expected:
Sturm trots gently.
Blitz sprints down the track.
Stella jumps the fence.

tasks.instruction: The classes Horse, Racehorse and Jumper are given. Write a function `los(figure)` that calls `figure.run()`. Call it for Racehorse("Blitz") and Jumper("Stella") one after the other.

validation.expected:
Blitz sprints down the track.
Stella jumps the fence.

The classes are given. Write your **own** class Spectator **without parents** with `run(self)` that prints The crowd applauds.. Call `run()` for a list with Racehorse("Blitz") and Spectator() one after the other (duck typing).

validation.expected:
Blitz sprints down the track.
The crowd applauds.

title: Extra Challenge 4: Everything Together
lessonSummary: Done: inheritance, dictionaries, randomness and JSON work together!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – dictionary of classes: the classes are given. Build `klassen = {"Racehorse": Racehorse, "Jumper": Jumper}` and create an object through the name `klassen["Racehorse"]("Blitz")`. Call `run()`.
Step 2 – randomness: the classes are given. Pick a class with `random.choice([Racehorse, Jumper])`, create an object from it and print `isinstance(object, Horse)` (True).

Step 3 – save as JSON: the classes are given. Create Racehorse("Blitz") and build `daten = {"typ": type(f).__name__, "name": f.name}` (`type(f).__name__` gives the class name as text). Print `json.dumps(daten)`.

Step 4 – load JSON: the classes and the text `text = '{"typ": "Racehorse", "name": "Blitz"}'` are given. Read it with `json.loads`, look up the class in the dictionary `klassen` and rebuild the object. Call `run()`.
